verdict.rationale: Gmail's own filters evaluate incoming mail against criteria such as sender, subject, or size, then automatically add or remove labels or forward the message to a specified address. That covers the rule-based routing half of the story. Nothing in the evidence shows assigning a conversation to a teammate or tracking ownership; delegation gives someone access to a whole account, which is a different control. Missing for 10: per-conversation assignment to teammates, explicit ownership/assignee tracking, team-shared routing rules, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a team-lead, I can assign conversations to teammates and route incoming mail with rules so ownership is explicit

citations.quote: When a message matches, filters automatically trigger actions such as adding or removing labels, or forwarding the email to a specified address.
Advanced rules configured for an account that evaluate incoming messages against specific matching criteria (like sender, subject, or size).
